subject.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs

question: Should file-transfer policy treat `~\` as the Windows spelling of the existing home-relative `~/` syntax for evaluated node paths?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and proven, but it intentionally changes the meaning of persisted file-access policy strings and can activate previously ineffective allow rules.

options.title: Accept Windows home syntax
options.body: Merge the focused normalization change and make `~\` equivalent to `~/` across allow and deny policy entries.

options.title: Retain the shipped grammar
options.body: Keep bare `~` and `~/` as the only home-relative forms and require Windows operators to use that canonical syntax.

recommendation.title: Accept Windows home syntax
recommendation.body: Merge the focused normalization change and make `~\` equivalent to `~/` across allow and deny policy entries.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original feature and have recent ownership signals across the extension's commands, helpers, and documentation.
